Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The honouring of obligations and commitments by Azerbaijan', expressed concern that recently adopted amendments to the Criminal Code and the Administrative Code had increased penalties for the organisers of, and participants in, unauthorised gatherings.

Resolution 1917 (2013) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that, considering the authorities' ongoing blanket ban on protests in the Baku city centre, the amendments increasing penalties for organisers of and participants in unauthorised gatherings were likely to have a further negative impact on freedom of assembly and freedom of expression.
Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe, titled 'The functioning of democratic institutions in Azerbaijan', was adopted on 23 June 2015.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that the lack of independence of the judiciary remains a concern in Azerbaijan, where the executive branch is alleged to continue to exert undue influence.
Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that dubiously motivated criminal prosecutions and disproportionate sentences remain a concern in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that fairness of trials, equality of arms and respect for the presumption of innocence are major concerns in Azerbaijan.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe stated that it was alarmed by reports by human rights defenders and international NGOs, confirmed by the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights, concerning the increase in criminal prosecutions against NGO leaders, journalists, lawyers and others who express critical opinions, based on alleged charges in relation to their work.

Resolution 2062 (2015) of the Parliamentary Assembly of the Council of Europe called on the Azerbaijani authorities to end the systemic harassment of those who are critical of the government and to release those wrongfully detained.

The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that the overall human rights situation in Azerbaijan has deteriorated continuously over the last few years, with growing intimidation and repression and intensification of the practice of criminal prosecution of NGO leaders, human rights defenders, journalists and other civil society representatives.
The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that peaceful protesters have been effectively banned from demonstrating in central Baku since 2006.

The European Parliament in its Resolution (2015/2840(RSP)) of 10 September 2015 emphasised that new, harsh fines and longer periods of administrative detention for those who organise or participate in unauthorised public gatherings have recently been introduced in Azerbaijan.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', referred to a decrease of public protests in Azerbaijan due to the harshening from 1 January 2013 of penalties for breach of rules on organisation and holding of peaceful assemblies.

Amnesty International in its Report of May 2014, titled 'Behind Bars: Silencing Dissent in Azerbaijan', emphasised that those who have called for public protest in Azerbaijan have been dealt with harshly, with criminal proceedings initiated against them under fabricated charges.

In a public statement of 7 March 2014, titled 'Azerbaijan: Opposition party loses HQ after explosion and sees seven members arrested within 2 weeks', Amnesty International reported on numerous detentions and arrests of activists of the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan during late February and early March 2014.
Amnesty International's public statement of 7 March 2014 reported on an explosion which occurred on 3 March 2014 in the basement of a building housing the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan.

Amnesty International's public statement of 7 March 2014 reported on allegations by the owner of the property housing the Popular Front Party of Azerbaijan that prior to the explosion he had been pressured to evict the party.
